clue.text: Formal coat is dull at back

indicators.note: back says the words dull and at, taken together, are read from end to start

parts.note: drab means dull, lacking colour or interest
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's formal coat looks drab from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole run DRABAT round to give the answer; 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a short sleeveless tunic worn by heralds over armour, a ceremonial garment.

clue.text: Goddess with a heavenly body, note

parts.note: taken as written
a star is a heavenly body
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A goddess associated with a star and a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte was the Phoenician goddess of fertility and love, a deity of the ancient Near East.

clue.text: Went straight, although wearing old convict gear?

definitions.meaning: moved in a direct line, as an arrow flies
British convicts once wore uniforms printed with broad arrows, so they were literally marked with arrows

explanation.walkthrough: 'Went straight' suggests a reformed criminal, tying neatly to the convict gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying like an arrow means travelling directly; old prison clothing bore broad-arrow markings.

clue.text: Son received into respectable family line

indicators.note: received into says one letter is taken inside the word for respectable

parts.note: decent means respectable

explanation.surface: A son is welcomed into a respectable family line.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent means ancestry, the lineage one is born from.

clue.text: Very warm longs? Exactly the opposite!

definitions.text: Very warm longs? Exactly the opposite!

parts.words: Very warm longs? Exactly the opposite!
parts.note: the opposite of very warm long trousers would be hot but very short ones, which is what this garment is called

explanation.surface: A joke about trousers being the reverse of what you'd expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exactly the opposite' keeps 'very warm' and flips 'longs' to its opposite, giving very warm shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: These are very brief, tight shorts fashionable for women in the 1970s.

clue.text: Tradesman ready to sell more likely to survive?

parts.note: a product that is out has been released and is available to buy
fitter, as in survival of the fittest, means better able to survive

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper eager to trade is asked whether that improves his chances.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shopkeeper who sells clothing and equipment.

clue.text: Puppet on string should get laugh at last

parts.note: Punch is the puppet of Punch and Judy shows
a line is a length of string or cord

explanation.surface: A marionette dangling on its string ought to raise a laugh eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: PUNCH is the hook-nosed puppet of British seaside Punch and Judy shows. 'on' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The final line of a joke is the one meant to make the audience laugh.

clue.text: City —- no need to move here from mine?

definitions.text: City —- no need to move here from mine?

parts.words: City —- no need to move here from mine?
parts.note: the proverb about carrying coals to this northern English mining city means doing something pointless, so coal from a mine need not be sent there

explanation.surface: A question about whether a city needs goods brought from a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying coals to Newcastle' is a British idiom for a pointless errand, since the city was a coal-mining centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in north-east England famous for exporting coal from local mines.

clue.text: Extra on bill, to take tea in rush

indicators.note: to take says the word for rush takes another word inside it

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rush
char is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: An extra charge on the bill for grabbing a quick cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is everyday British slang for a cup of tea; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an additional fee added to a price or bill.

clue.text: Mix in jug

definitions.meaning: to blend by moving a spoon round
jug is slang for prison, as is the other sense here

explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to mix; stir is also slang for prison, like jug.

clue.text: Gentle light that helps restore calm mood?

parts.note: soft means gentle
in crosswords a light is an entry in the grid, its solution

explanation.surface: A gentle lamp that soothes the atmosphere in a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like illumination but is the crossword word for a grid entry. The biblical proverb says a mild reply turns away wrath.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbs says a mild reply turns away wrath, so a gentle response calms anger.

clue.text: Casually survey sound indicators of intellectual level?

indicators.note: sound says the word is heard rather than spelt, giving a word that is pronounced the same

parts.note: brows, as in highbrow and lowbrow, mark intellectual level

explanation.surface: Someone glances at a person's forehead to gauge their cleverness.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to look over things in a leisurely way.

clue.text: Real mess as husband is involved in motorway accident

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

indicators.note: is involved in says the husband letter is put inside the motorway and accident words

parts.note: a smash is a crash or accident

explanation.surface: A husband is caught up in a motorway pile-up, a real mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a London-to-Leeds motorway; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishmash is a confused jumble, a muddle.

clue.text: Is in charge of cutting early lead

parts.note: heads means leads or is in charge of
a tart remark is a sharp, cutting one

explanation.surface: A boss is in charge of reducing an early advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' looks like the insertion signal but is an adjective meaning sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage given at the outset, a lead held from the beginning.

clue.text: Tricky situation for consumer liable to get fingers burnt?

definitions.meaning: an awkward issue nobody wants to handle

definitions.text: for consumer liable to get fingers burnt?
definitions.meaning: literally, a just-baked spud is too warm for the eater to hold

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a controversial issue, like a scalding vegetable passed hand to hand.

clue.text: Leisurely outings to fish in Lake District area

parts.note: ambles are leisurely walks
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Gentle walks to go fishing in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link. The Lake District is a mountain and lake region of north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambleside is a town at the head of Windermere in Cumbria's lakeland.

clue.text: Cut the drones out

indicators.note: out says the letters are disordered, put out of place

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Get rid of the idle males in the hive.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut something is to make it less long, to curtail it.

clue.text: Fit American carrying soldier's equipment

indicators.note: carrying says the word for fit holds the soldier inside it

parts.note: apt means fit or suitable
a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

explanation.surface: A fit American carries a soldier's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus means the gear or instruments needed for a task.

clue.text: Lay to rest some uncertain terror

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Burying some vague dread to put it out of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter means to bury a body in a grave.

clue.text: About to take strike-successive poor scores unthinkable

indicators.note: About says the word for taking strike is turned backwards

parts.note: in cricket, to take strike is to bat
two noughts, ducks in cricket, look like OO

explanation.surface: A cricketer about to face the bowling makes two ducks in a row, unthinkable.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman facing the bowler is on strike, and a score of nought is a duck, written 0.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is forbidden by custom, not to be considered.

clue.text: In school, always keep working

indicators.note: In says the word for always sits inside the school

parts.note: the Perse is a well-known school in Cambridge
ever means always

explanation.surface: Advice to a pupil: in school, always keep at it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Perse School is an old independent school in Cambridge, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to continue steadily despite difficulty.

clue.text: This sort of act a sin

definitions.text: This sort of act a sin

indicators.note: sort of says the letters are sorted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A deed of this kind would count as sinful.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, a diabolical deed is indeed a sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish acts are wicked and sinful, belonging to the Devil.

clue.text: Tax bill up in surrounding city-state

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

indicators.note: surrounding says the word in goes round the turned bill

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A tax bill rises in a city-state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AC into CA, which IN then surrounds to make ICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican City is the papal enclave in Rome, the world's smallest sovereign state.

clue.text: Fillet to go round untidy hair

parts.note: to roll is to go round, turning over
a mop is a shaggy mass of hair

explanation.surface: A hairdresser is told to work round a messy head of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a pickled herring fillet rolled around onion.

clue.text: On appeal, reverse obvious run out

parts.note: overt means open, obvious

indicators.note: out says the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire's obvious run-out decision is reversed on appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A higher court may overturn, that is annul, a lower court's verdict.

clue.text: Stroke of the pen reducing gossip by 50%

indicators.note: reducing says the gossip word is cut down
by 50% says exactly half of the word for gossip is kept

parts.note: ...-tattle is idle gossip

explanation.surface: Cutting gossip in half with a stroke of the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A tittle is a small written mark, such as the dot over an i.

clue.text: After a deception, people divorce

parts.note: a lie is a deception
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: After deceit, a couple divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divorce' is a noun here, meaning separation.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienation means estrangement, a separation of people once close.

clue.text: Curry leaving five-piece band one short

indicators.note: one short says a letter is removed from the end of the band word

parts.note: a combo is a small band; it has five letters

explanation.surface: A curry restaurant losing one member of its five-piece band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curry' is the verb meaning to groom a horse, not the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To curry a horse is to groom it with a toothed tool.

clue.text: Love-poetry about affair too much of a good thing?

definitions.text: too much of a good thing?

parts.note: love is a nil score in tennis, written O

indicators.note: about says the poetry word goes round the affair word

parts.note: verse means poetry
a do is a party or affair

explanation.surface: Love poems about a romance are too much of a good thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An excessive dose of a drug, a harmful excess of something beneficial.

clue.text: Get a mouthful, having forty winks in church

indicators.note: in says the nap goes inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
forty winks is a nap

explanation.surface: Someone eats a snack after dozing in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A canape is a small savoury appetiser eaten in one bite.
